title: Balance CI test shards by recorded per-target timings
summary: Change `xtask test-shard` to assign test units to shards greedily, longest first, using durations from a small checked-in timings file under xtask/. Units with no timing fall back to the current sorted index-modulo split. Add an xtask command that rewrites the timings file from a local run. The audience is CI maintainers, who want the slowest shard near the mean.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests for balance, fallback and partition; the full test suite and clippy must pass.
Reuse cargo metadata and cargo test; no new sharding tool.
Criteria check the measured shard totals and the partition by running tests.
The verifier runs the cargo commands.
Docs and comments explain the timings file and how to refresh it.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read xtask/src/shard.rs (entry point `command` runs `cargo metadata`, then `plan_units` builds the sorted unit list, then `select` keeps units where sorted index % n == k, then runs `cargo test -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit or prints with --dry-run), xtask/src/main.rs (dispatch of `test-shard` and `walltime` subcommands plus the usage text), and xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs (an oracle built from cargo metadata, `check_cover`, and `shard_units` calling the built binary with --dry-run). The shard.rs unit tests are in-module because xtask is a binary crate, so the fixture-based balance and missing-target tests belong there, while the integration partition test stays unchanged. Resolution order to keep: plan_units first, then timing lookup by `Unit::line()` key, then greedy assignment, then fallback. The crates/ records validation (crates/athena-data/src/records.rs `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord`) only covers files under records/, so a timings file at xtask/ is outside it and no round-trip test is needed. The property is measured directly by summing fixture durations per shard from the real `select` output, not through a stand-in.

The timings file is xtask/shard-timings.txt (one `<package> <selector> <seconds>` line per unit, or equivalent JSON). The update command, `xtask shard-timings`, runs each unit with timing and rewrites the file; it is documented in USAGE and main.rs. Only the file name is open to change.

The unit key is the existing `Unit::line()`. Mixed assignment: units without timings are placed by the old index-modulo rule on the sorted list of untimed units, then added to the shard loads. The result must be deterministic, and ties break by unit order so `--dry-run` output stays stable.
Not a refusal-rule change, so no refused-readings percentage applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test uses a fixture timings map and calls the real selection for n=6. It asserts that the largest per-shard duration total is at most 1.25 times the mean, and that each unit appears in exactly one shard.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A shard.rs unit test includes a unit absent from the fixture timings and asserts that it is assigned to exactly one shard, with all units still covered.
Run `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`. The existing ci_shards partition tests pass, including `shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target`, with the real checked-in timings file.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace`. All pass.

xtask/src/shard.rs sorts timed units by descending duration and places each on the currently least-loaded shard. The checked-in timings file is parsed with a clear error for a malformed line. A new xtask subcommand that regenerates the file is wired in xtask/src/main.rs and listed in the usage text.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that describes timing-balanced sharding, the timings file and the update command.
The checked-in timings file covers the current workspace test units, so the real shards are balanced rather than all falling back.

out_of_scope: Adding a sharding tool such as cargo-nextest
Splitting individual tests within a target
